auth.title: Access Tokens Guide
highlights:
# Access Tokens Guide

The platform supports the following access token types. The type you use depends on who uses your application, and whether you are a partner.

- If you are a direct developer, meaning only you or your business accesses your own data, use a System User access token.
- If you are a Tech Provider, use a Business Integration System User access token.
- If you are a solution partner, use System User access tokens to share your line of credit with newly onboarded customers, and Business Integration System User access tokens for everything else.

## System user access tokens

System user access tokens ("system tokens") represent you, your business, organization, or people within your business or organization. The main advantage of these tokens is that they are long-lived and can represent automated services within your business that don't require any user input.

System tokens rely on system users. Most endpoints check if the user identified by the token has access to the queried resource. If the user doesn't have access to the resource, the system rejects the request with error code `200` (not to be confused with HTTP status code `200`).

System users can be admins or employees.

### Admin system users {#admin-system-users}

By default, admin system users have full access to all WhatsApp accounts (WAACs), Messaging accounts, and their assets owned by or shared with you or your business portfolio.

Admin system users are useful if your app needs access to all of the business portfolio's assets, without having to manually grant business asset access to each asset whenever it is created, or shared with your business portfolio.

You can override an admin system user's default business asset access by granting partial access per account. Grant it separately for each WhatsApp account and each Messaging account. See Business Asset Access to learn how to set and override access.

### Employee system users {#employee-system-users}

Employee system users must be granted access to the individual WhatsApp accounts and Messaging accounts that are owned by, or shared with, your business portfolio. If your app only needs access to a few accounts that you own, an employee system user should be sufficient.

Once created, you must grant Partial or Full business asset access for both accounts the system user needs to work with: the WhatsApp account and the Messaging account. Access to the Messaging account alone is not sufficient.

How the grant is applied differs by surface:

- API. Granting business asset access on a Messaging account also applies that grant to the WhatsApp account it is linked to. This cascade exists because the WhatsApp account has no Graph API endpoints of its own yet. Treat it as interim behavior rather than something to depend on.
- Meta Business Suite. The panel does not cascade. Assign the system user to the WhatsApp account and to the Messaging account explicitly.

### Generate system user access tokens {#generating-system-user-access-tokens}

To generate a system token, access the Business settings panel and then click System Users:

Click the +Add button, and in the Create system user window that appears, enter a system user name and assign it an Admin or Employee role:

Once you create the admin system user, it appears in the list of system users. Click the system user's name to display the asset assignment overlay:

Click the Assign assets button to display the Select assets and assign permissions window:

Select your app and grant your system user the Manage app permission, then click the Assign assets button to confirm and dismiss the window.

Back in the System Users panel, reload the page to confirm that your system user has been granted Full control of your app. Granting the permissions may take a few minutes, so reload the page if your app doesn't appear as an assigned asset. Once the asset has been assigned, it should look like this:

Once you see that your system user has been granted full control of your app, in the asset assignment overlay, click the Generate token button. In the window that appears, select your app, choose a token expiration preference, and assign your app these three Graph API permissions:

- `business_management`
- `whatsapp_business_management`
- `whatsapp_business_messaging`

You can search for `business` to find these permissions quickly:

Click the Generate token button and copy the token when it appears.

## Business integration system user access tokens

Business Integration System User access tokens ("business tokens") are scoped to individual onboarded customers and should be used by Tech Providers and solution partners when accessing onboarded customer data.

These tokens are useful for apps that perform programmatic, automated actions on customer Messaging accounts, without having to rely on input from an app user, or requiring future re-authentication.

To generate a Business Integration System User access token, you must implement Embedded Signup (configured with Facebook Login for Businesses) and exchange the code returned to you when a customer completes the flow.

See Embedded Signup and Business Integration System User access tokens to learn more about these tokens and how to generate them.

## User access tokens

Although User access tokens are supported and can be used by all app developers, you typically only use them when you first use the App Dashboard to send your first test message. As you develop your app, however, you switch to a System User access token (and eventually a Business Integration System User access token, if you are a Tech Provider or a partner). This is because user access tokens expire quickly, so you have to keep generating a new one every few hours.

There are several ways to generate a User access token:

- Access the App Dashboard > WhatsApp > API setup panel. This panel always generates a new User access token whenever you visit it. The token is automatically scoped to your user, since you are signed into your developer account when you access the panel.
- Use Graph API Explorer.
- Implement Facebook Login.

## Use tokens in requests

When making API requests, include your token in an authorization request header, preceded by `Bearer`. For example:

```html
curl 'https://graph.facebook.com/v27.0/102290129340398/message_templates' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer EAAJB...'

```

## Token format

Access tokens are opaque strings. A full token looks like this:

```
EAAJBsbCmS80BO4hZBf5xYKFaFW7kVMNxAWzIInZB7q1PuZCLiEqKh3gZDZD

```

Tokens can vary in length, and their internal structure and characteristics can change over time. Do not parse, decode, or make assumptions about the format of an access token — treat it as an opaque string. Use a variable-length data type without a specific maximum size to store access tokens.

## Business asset access

After creating a system user, you must set business asset access levels. Many endpoints require the system user whose token is included in API requests to have either Partial or Full business asset access to both the WhatsApp account and the Messaging account being queried (or their assets). If the system user doesn't have this access, these endpoints return error code `200` (not to be confused with HTTP status code `200`).

...

The cascade is interim behavior that exists only until the WhatsApp account has API

auth.title: Using Authorization Tokens for the WhatsApp Business Platform
highlights:
December 5, 2022

# Using Authorization Tokens for the WhatsApp Business Platform

#### By Rashed Talukder

The WhatsApp Business Platform makes it easy to send WhatsApp messages to your customers and automate replies. Here, we’ll explore authentication using the Cloud API, hosted by Meta.

We’ll start with generating and using a temporary access token and then replace it with a permanent access token. This tutorial assumes you’re building a server-side application and won’t need additional steps to keep your WhatsApp application secrets securely stored.

...

Note that you have a temporary access token. For security reasons, the token expires in less than 24 hours. However, you can use it for now to test accessing the API. Later, we’ll cover how to generate a permanent access token that your server applications can use. Also, note your app’s phone number ID because you’ll need it soon.

Click the dropdown under the To field, and then click Manage phone number list.

In the popup that appears, enter the phone number of a WhatsApp account to send test messages to.

Then, scroll further down the dashboard page and you’ll see an example curl call that looks similar to this:

```
curl -i -X POST https://graph.facebook.com/v13.0/<YOUR PHONE NUMBER ID>/messages -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR ACCESS TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "messaging_product": "whatsapp", "to": "<PHONE NUMBER TO MESSAGE>", "type": "template", "template": { "name": "hello_world", \"language\": { \"code\": \"en_US\" } } }'
```

Note that the Meta for Developers platform inserts your app’s phone number ID and access token instead of the <YOUR PHONE NUMBER ID> and <YOUR ACCESS TOKEN> placeholders shown above. If you have`curl` installed, paste the command into your terminal and run it. You should receive a “hello world” message in WhatsApp on your test device.

If you’d prefer, you can convert the curl request into an HTTP request in your programming language by simply creating a POST request that sets the Authorization and Content-Type headers as shown above, including the JSON payload in the request body.

Since this post is about authentication, let’s focus on that. Notice that you’ve included your app’s access token in the Authorization header. For any request to the API, you must set the Authorization header to`Bearer <YOUR ACCESS TOKEN>`.

Remember that you must use your token instead of the placeholder. Using bearer tokens will be familiar if you’ve worked with JWT or OAuth2 tokens before. If you’ve never seen one before, a bearer token is essentially a random secret string that you, as the bearer of the token, can present to an API to prove you’re allowed to access it.

Failure to include this header causes the API to return a 401 Unauthorized response code.

### Creating a Permanent Access Token

Knowing that you need to use a bearer token in the Authorization header of an HTTP request is helpful, but it’s not enough. The only access token you’ve seen so far is temporary. Chances are that you want your app to access the API for more than 24 hours, so you need to generate a longer-lasting access token.

Fortunately, the Meta for Developers platform makes this easy. All you need to do is add a System User to your business account to obtain an access token you can use to continue accessing the API. To create a system user, do the following:

Go to Business Settings.

- Copy and save your token.
- Click Generate New Token.
- Select the whatsapp_business_messaging permission.
- Name the system user, choose Admin as the user role, and click Create System User.
- Click Add.
- Below Users, click System Users.
- Select the business account your app is associated with.

Your access token is a random string of letters and numbers. Now, try re-running the earlier request using the token you just created instead of the temporary one:

```
curl -i -X POST https://graph.facebook.com/v13.0/<YOUR PHONE NUMBER ID>/messages -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR ACCESS TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "messaging_product": "whatsapp", "to": "<PHONE NUMBER TO MESSAGE>", "type": "template", "template": { "name": "hello_world", \"language\": { \"code\": \"en_US\" } } }'
```

Your test device should receive a second hello message sent via the API.

## Best Practices for Managing Access Tokens

It’s important to remember that you should never embed an App Access Token in a mobile or desktop application. These tokens are only for use in server-side applications that communicate with the API. Safeguard them the same way you would any other application secrets, like your database credentials, as anyone with your token has access to the API as your business.

If your application runs on a cloud services provider like AWS, Azure, GCP, or others, those platforms have tools to securely store app secrets. Alternatively there are freely-available secret stores like Vault or Conjur. While any of these options may work for you, it’s important to evaluate your options and choose what works best for your setup. At the very least, consider storing access tokens in environment variables and not in a database or a file where they’re easy to find during a data breach.

highlights:
## WhatsApp Business Platform Ecosystem

The ecosystem is split into two types of partners

### Tech Partners

Tech Partners are third party developers who build value added solutions on top of the WhatsApp Business Platform. These solutions can be offered independently or as part of a joint solution with a Solution Partner.*

Third Party Developers → Tech Provider → Tech Partner

* Note: Third party developers must onboard first as a Tech Provider before upgrading to Tech Partner.

### Solution Partners

Solution Partners offer end-to-end solutions for businesses which includes driving awareness of WhatsApp Business Platform solutions, providing integration services, and offering customer support. Only Solution Partners can extend a line of credit to businesses for payment.

Tech Partners and Solution Partners play different roles in helping businesses deploy solutions on the WhatsApp Business Platform. The below chart shows where each type differs:

 Solution Partner 

 Direct access to call WhatsApp Business Platform 

 Permission to manage business's account and perform action on behalf of business (e.g. send messages, manage templates) 

 Can onboard businesses using Embedded Signup 

 Eligibility for partner program incentives 

 Manage billing on behalf of business through line of credit sharing 

Tech Providers who meet specified requirements will be eligible to self-initiate the Tech Partner upgrade process.

## Why become a Tech Provider?

Build and launch solutions on WhatsApp easier and faster.

### Simple client onboarding

- Onboard clients to your solution using embedded signup. This helps to improve customer onboarding times, speed to market, and gives more visibility to your business and solution. Learn more.

gate.title: Frequently Asked Questions | Get answers from WhatsApp for Business
highlights:
Q: How is the WhatsApp Business Platform different from the WhatsApp Business app?      

A: The WhatsApp Business app ​​is for small businesses to communicate with customers from a single device through a free-to-download app. The Business app enables businesses to reach hundreds of customers, is free to use and offers limited customization and integration with other tools.

The WhatsApp Business Platform enables medium and large businesses to chat with customers at scale through programmatic access to WhatsApp. Businesses also get access to rich messaging features on the platform such as the ability to send media with messages and add quick reply buttons. The Platform enables businesses to reach millions of customers at a time, and integrate with the rest of their technology stack. Businesses pay per conversation they have with their customers and the first 1,000 conversations per month are free.

  Q: What are the options for integrating with the WhatsApp Business Platform?      

A: Business can choose from:

1. Directly accessing the WhatsApp Business Platform by signing up here. You must be a developer in order to do so as this requires being able to call our APIs and set up webhooks.
2. Accessing the Platform by working with one of our approved Business Solution Providers.

  Q: How should a business decide to use the platform directly, or to work with an integration partner?      

A: Businesses with in-house developers who can directly call our APIs may be interested in signing up directly. If you are not a developer, or would like to connect WhatsApp to the rest of your technology stack, such as an omnichannel inbox, customer support software, or a bot platform, you may prefer to work with one of our partners.

  Q: Can a developer sign up and offer platform access to other businesses?      

A: At this time, developers can access our APIs on behalf of their own business only. If you are interested in offering API access to other businesses, or becoming a partner, please join our waitlist.

  Q: Is it possible to use an on-premises API, if we don’t want to use the Cloud API?      

A: If you are interested in an on-premises option, please work with one of our partners. We are not enabling direct access to the on-premises API.

  Q: What are the options for technical support with the WhatsApp Business Platform?      

A: All businesses and developers directly accessing our platform have access to our Direct Support portal where you can submit questions. If you are working with a partner, they can submit tickets on your behalf.

  Q: How much does it cost to use the WhatsApp Business Platform?      

A:

- Meta charges businesses for the messages they send to users. There is no additional fee to access our platform directly. Partners may charge additional fees based on value-added services or technologies they provide.
- Beginning on July 1, 2025, Meta charges businesses on a per-message basis to deliver messages to WhatsApp users. Rates depend on the category of the message being delivered: marketing, utility, authentication, service, or Meta Business Agent. 

- For marketing, utility, and authentication: Meta charges for message delivery, and rates differ by category and market. 
- For service messages: Effective October 1, 2026, Meta also charges for these messages on a per-message basis. For every business phone number, the first 1,000 service messages are free each month to enable businesses to offer an always-on channel to connect with their customers. Meta will charge as of the 1,001st service message per published rates.
- For Meta Business Agent: Meta charges one token-based charge that encompasses message delivery and the AI agent usage. 

  Q: What billing options are available for the WhatsApp Business Platform?      

A: We have a few billing options available.

For most message types, if you access our platform directly, you can pay via credit card or via a credit line with Meta (to be invoiced monthly). We recommend a credit line for businesses with an expected spend of over $10,000 USD per month. Learn more here. For businesses in India, Meta is introducing UPI (Unified Payments Interface) as a pre-payment method.

If you work with one of our Solution Providers, we will bill them directly for your usage.

For Meta Business Agent, Meta charges businesses directly, even if you work with one of our Solution Providers to access our platform. Learn more here. 

The applicable VAT, GST, sales tax or any other applicable tax will be included in your invoice.

gate.title: Pricing on the WhatsApp Business Platform
highlights:
Per-message pricing is live and now applies to businesses for whom it is July 1, 2025 or later, based on their WABA timezone.

# Pricing on the WhatsApp Business Platform

This document explains how pricing works on the WhatsApp Business Platform.

## Cloud API and MM Lite API

To align with industry-standards, effective July 1, 2025, we now charge on a per-message basis:

- Rates vary based on the template's category and the recipient WhatsApp phone number's country calling code.
- We only charge when a template message is delivered (`"type":"template"`).

We provide value to businesses in several ways:

- All messages are free for 72 hours, including template messages, if sent within an open free entry point window.
- You can unlock lower rates for utility and authentication template messages, based on messaging volume.
- Utility templates delivered within an open customer service window are free.
- All non-template messages are free (`"type":"text"`,`"type":"image"`, etc.). These can only be sent within an open customer service window. See Sending messages for a list of message types.

Our pricing explainer PDF outlines how we charge, and the various ways we provide value to businesses, in PDF form:

Pricing Explainer PDF

## Message template categories

Unlike non-template messages, template messages are the only message type that can be sent outside of a customer service window. Templates can be categorized as:

- Authentication
- Utility
- Marketing

See Template categorization to learn how template categorization works.

### Template messages vs. non-template messages

| Is it billable? | Message type | Message category | When can it be sent? | Delivered outside CSW* | Delivered inside CSW* | Delivered inside FEP** window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Template messages | Marketing | Anytime | Yes | Yes | No |
| Authentication | Anytime | Yes | Yes | No |
| Utility | Anytime | Yes | No | No |
| Non-template (free-form) messages | Service | Only inside an open CSW* | N/A | No | No |

* Customer service window** Free entry point window

Businesses are responsible for reviewing the category assigned to their approved templates. Whenever a template is used, a business accepts the charges associated with the category applied to the template at time of use.

...

## Rates

Rates vary based on template category, volume tier, and country/region rate.

### Rate cards and volume tiers

These rate cards reflect our current rates and volume tiers, effective July 1, 2025, based on WhatsApp Business Account timezone. This information is also available interactively on our WhatsApp Business website.

...

- If you respond within 24 hours using any type of message, the message will be free, and a Free Entry Point ("FEP") window will be opened, starting from the time when you responded.
- A 24-hour customer service window is opened (as normal).

FEP windows remain open for 72 hours. While open, you can send any type of message to the user at no charge. Note, however, that the customer service window is independent of the FEP window, so if the customer service window closes, you will only be able to send template messages.

mcp.title: Meta Puts AI Agents Into The WhatsApp Business Setup Layer
highlights:
M

...

16 Sep 2026  15:40 IST

...

Meta is now putting part of that process in the hands of AI agents. The company has introduced WhatsApp Business Tools MCP, a Model Context Protocol server that connects AI coding agents to the WhatsApp Business Platform. Meta's developer documentation lists the tool as a way for agents to set up and manage parts of WhatsApp Business, including accounts, phone numbers, templates, and testing.

The more significant change is where the agent is being allowed to operate. This is not simply an AI assistant answering questions about an API. The agent can perform actions against the business messaging environment, subject to user authentication and permissions.

## The Setup Work Moves Into The Agent

Today, setting up a WhatsApp Business integration can require developers to move between Meta's Developer Console, Business Manager, API documentation, and their development environment.

Meta's new approach brings several of those steps into an agent-led workflow. A developer can describe what needs to be configured, while the agent handles the relevant platform operations.

The tool can create a WhatsApp Business account, add and verify a phone number, register it for the Cloud API, and check whether required terms have been accepted. It can also identify missing requirements such as payment methods or Business Verification and direct the user to the relevant step.

That matters because the friction in enterprise integrations often isn't the API call itself. It is the sequence around it: permissions, account state, verification, configuration, and testing. AI agents are increasingly being positioned to handle that layer.

## From Templates To Webhook Testing

Meta's tool goes beyond initial onboarding. Developers can use the agent to create or edit WhatsApp message templates and check their approval status. It can also support test messages and webhook configuration, including callback URLs and field subscriptions.

...

It can also interact with parts of the platform that the application depends on.

...

## Human Authorization Remains The Control Point

Meta says users sign in through Facebook Login for Business and provide specific permissions. The system checks whether the user is an administrator of the relevant app and confirms the connected business and required terms.

Meta also says read operations run under the user's own viewer context and that tool invocations are logged. Actions that change account state require an authenticated person rather than an app-level credential. 

The value of an agent in this model comes from its ability to take action. The same capability creates a governance requirement: businesses need to know which account an agent can access, what permissions it has, and which actions require a person to approve them.

For enterprise teams, the question therefore shifts from whether an AI agent can complete a configuration task to whether the organization is comfortable giving the agent that level of operational access.

...

WhatsApp Business Tools MCP also sits alongside Meta's broader Meta Social Technologies MCP. The latter is designed to help developers discover Graph API endpoints, search documentation, and troubleshoot errors. WhatsApp Business Tools MCP is more focused on the WhatsApp Business environment itself, including onboarding, templates, testing, and configuration.

...

## Early Release, Narrower Than Production Automation

There is also an important limitation to the announcement. Meta says WhatsApp Business Tools MCP is intended for development and testing workflows rather than production messaging at scale. Availability is also being rolled out gradually, meaning the feature may not yet be accessible to every developer. 

That makes the announcement less about replacing existing enterprise messaging infrastructure and more about changing how developers interact with it.

mcp.title: WhatsApp Business MCP: let AI agents run your WhatsApp
highlights:
## What the WhatsApp Business MCP actually does

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It’s a standard way to plug an AI agent directly into a service, so the agent can take real actions instead of just chatting about them. Stripe, PayPal, GitHub, and Slack all have MCP servers you can already try. Now Meta built one for WhatsApp.

The WhatsApp Business MCP connects your AI agent to the WhatsApp Business Platform. You describe what you want in plain English. The agent handles the rest.

Before this launch, setting up WhatsApp Business messaging meant bouncing between four different tools: the developer console, Meta’s Business Manager, the API reference, and your code editor. Tedious. Error-prone. Easy to abandon halfway.

Now the agent can do all of this for you:

- Create your WhatsApp Business account and add your phone number
- Verify and register the number so it’s ready to send messages
- Write message templates and submit them for Meta’s approval
- Edit templates that got rejected and resubmit them
- Configure webhooks so customer replies reach your CRM or inbox
- Send test messages and flag anything configured wrong

That last part matters more than it sounds. Meta’s own announcement points out that things like an unsigned terms of service or a missing payment method used to “quietly fail.” Your messages wouldn’t send, and nothing told you why. The agent checks for that stuff before it bites you.

Noticed what’s missing from that list? Sending your actual customer campaigns. The MCP server handles setup and configuration, not day-to-day marketing. You’ll still run campaigns from a tool like the WhatsApp Business app or an API integration.

...

Claude Code users get the simplest setup. One command connects the WhatsApp Business MCP server:

```
claude mcp add --transport http whatsapp_business_tools https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools
```

After that, type `/mcp` inside your Claude session and pick whatsapp_business_tools from the list.

En lugar de pasar entre la consola de desarrolladores, el Administrador de empresas y la referencia de la API, usted le pide al agente que haga la configuración. Esta guía explica, con la documentación de la propia Meta, qué hace el servidor y dónde termina su alcance.

En resumen: es una herramienta de configuración y pruebas para quienes desarrollan sobre la API. No sirve para atender a los clientes. Si su equipo atiende soporte o ventas por WhatsApp, sigue haciendo falta un lugar donde lleguen las conversaciones, se asignen y se respondan.

## Qué es el servidor

- Servidor: WhatsApp Business Tools, en `https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools`, un servidor remoto sobre Streamable HTTP.
- Clientes que documenta Meta: Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http ...` y luego `/mcp` para iniciar sesión), Claude Desktop (Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector), la aplicación OpenAI Codex y ChatGPT. Los clientes que solo ejecutan servidores locales pueden usar el puente `mcp-remote`.
- Inicio de sesión: OAuth con su cuenta de desarrollador de Meta. Debe iniciar sesión de nuevo cada vez que reinicie el cliente.
- Disponibilidad: Meta indica que se está habilitando de forma gradual, por lo que puede que aún no esté disponible para todos, y que está en versión beta, así que el conjunto de herramientas puede cambiar.

Si el protocolo le resulta nuevo, empiece por MCP para mensajería con clientes.

## Las herramientas que lista Meta

Todas las herramientas llevan el prefijo `whatsapp_biz_`. Agrupadas por tarea:

| Tarea | Herramientas |
| --- | --- |
| Consulta | `whatsapp_biz_businesses`, `whatsapp_biz_accounts`, `whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers` |
| Alta de números de teléfono | `whatsapp_biz_add_phone_number`, `whatsapp_biz_send_verification_code`, `whatsapp_biz_verify_phone_number`, `whatsapp_biz_register_phone_number` |
| Plantillas de mensaje | `whatsapp_biz_list_templates`, `whatsapp_biz_get_template`, `whatsapp_biz_create_template`, `whatsapp_biz_update_template`, `whatsapp_biz_delete_template` |
| Mensajería | `whatsapp_biz_send_message` (pide confirmar el destinatario antes de enviar) |
| Webhooks | `whatsapp_biz_configure_webhooks`, `whatsapp_biz_subscribe_webhook` |
| Configuración de la cuenta | `whatsapp_biz_configure_payments`, `whatsapp_biz_verify_business`, `whatsapp_biz_system_user_token` |

Los ejemplos de Meta son peticiones sencillas: «List the businesses I can manage on WhatsApp» o «Create a marketing template named order_update in en_US». La mayoría de las herramientas trabajan a nivel de una sola empresa, así que una sesión suele empezar listando sus empresas. La herramienta del token de usuario del sistema solo devuelve un enlace; el token lo genera usted mismo en la Configuración de la empresa.

## Permisos y seguridad

El servidor solicita tres permisos OAuth:

- `business_management`: encontrar las empresas que seleccionó durante el consentimiento y actuar sobre ellas
- `whatsapp_business_management`: administrar cuentas de WhatsApp, números de teléfono, plantillas y webhooks
- `whatsapp_business_messaging`: enviar mensajes desde los números registrados

En la pantalla de consentimiento usted elige las empresas y aplicaciones que comparte, y puede revocar el acceso en Configuración, Integraciones de empresa en Facebook. Meta afirma que las lecturas se ejecutan con su propio contexto de usuario, que cada invocación queda registrada y que las acciones que modifican algo requieren a una persona autenticada, no una credencial a nivel de aplicación. Las solicitudes tienen un límite de frecuencia por usuario y por herramienta.

## Lo que necesita antes

El servidor no se salta las reglas de Meta. Para poder registrar un número o enviar un mensaje necesita:

1. Acceso de administrador (rol MANAGE) a la empresa.
2. Una aplicación habilitada para WhatsApp que usted administre, conectada a esa empresa. Ser administrador de la empresa no basta.
3. Los Términos de servicio de la WhatsApp Business Cloud API aceptados. El envío de mensajes y el registro de números quedan bloqueados hasta que un administrador los acepte.
4. Un método de pago y la verificación de empresa. El anuncio de Meta dice que estos pasos suelen fallar sin avisar, y el servidor los comprueba desde el inicio.

Cuando falta algo, la herramienta devuelve un error que explica la solución y enlaza a la página correcta.

## Lo que no hace

- No es para tráfico de producción. Meta lo describe como una herramienta para desarrollo y pruebas, no para envíos a gran escala.
- El texto libre sigue la regla de 24 horas. Fuera de la ventana de atención al cliente debe enviar una plantilla aprobada, igual que con cualquier llamada a la API.
- No tiene bandeja de entrada. No guarda el historial de conversaciones, no deriva un chat al agente correcto, no aplica horarios de atención ni traspasa de una IA a una persona.
- No cambia la facturación. Meta sigue cobrando los mensajes por categoría y país; consulte los precios de la API de WhatsApp Business.

## Cuándo es útil y cuándo no

Es útil para un desarrollador o una agencia que configura muchos números y plantillas, revisa por qué no se dispara un webhook o quiere confirmar una integración de punta a punta con un mensaje de prueba real. Las plantillas son un buen ejemplo: redactar una primera versión con un agente es rápido, pero Meta revisa cada plantilla y un texto adecuado a la categoría importa más que la velocidad. Nuestros ejemplos de plantillas de mensaje muestran qué pasa la revisión.

No es la herramienta adecuada cuando el objetivo es atender a clientes: recibir respuestas, contestar dentro de la ventana de 24 horas, asignar un chat, guardar notas, enviar campañas a contactos con opt-in (consentimiento). Para eso conecta su propia cuenta de WhatsApp Business a una plataforma.

mcp.title: Meta launches WhatsApp Business MCP server for automated AI agent setup – GenAI Daily
highlights:
## Dedicated server simplifies WhatsApp Business messaging integration

Meta introduced a WhatsApp Business Tools MCP server this week, an implementation of the Model Context Protocol that connects AI coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, Codex and ChatGPT directly to the WhatsApp Business Platform. Rather than opening the Developer Console or Business Manager, a developer can now describe what they need in a chat window and have the agent carry out the work directly against Meta’s systems.

The server is built to handle the early, repetitive steps of onboarding: creating a company’s WhatsApp Business account, adding and verifying a phone number, registering the account for access to the Cloud API, and checking that the business meets WhatsApp’s Terms of Service before it is allowed to send messages. This updated workflow eliminates the need to manually toggle between multiple Meta tools and API documentation, directly reducing the operational friction previously involved in setting up the service.

Meta frames the change as a shift from clicking through consoles to describing intent, with the agent translating a plain-language request such as “set up WhatsApp Business messaging for this company and verify the phone number” into the sequence of API calls that would previously have been assembled by hand.

## AI agents manage templates, message testing, and silent configuration failures

Beyond initial setup, businesses can hand the agent ongoing messaging work. A team can describe a message template it wants, such as a shipping confirmation or an appointment reminder, and have the agent draft, submit or edit it, rather than building templates by hand inside Business Manager. The agent can also send test messages and exercise webhooks to confirm that integrations are firing correctly before anything goes live to customers.

Meta says the tool is also meant to catch problems that used to fail silently, such as a lapsed Terms of Service acceptance, an expired payment method, or a stalled Business Verification request, any of which can quietly stop messages from being delivered without an obvious error appearing in a dashboard. A companion server, the Meta Social Technologies MCP, can be used during the same setup process to look up API endpoints, search documentation and help diagnose errors, giving an agent a way to troubleshoot a failed step without the developer leaving the conversation.

mcp.title: Meta gives AI agents access to WhatsApp Business tools | Qatar Living

Now, the developer can describe tasks to the AI agent to take over a large part of the setup steps.

The feature is based on WhatsApp Business Tools MCP, a server based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) protocol that connects AI programming agents such as Claude, Cursor, Codex, and ChatGPT, to the WhatsApp Business platform.

The agent can perform tasks that include creating a WhatsApp Business account, adding and verifying a phone number, registering an account to access the Cloud API, reviewing terms of service, preparing and testing messages, creating and editing message templates, testing Webhooks, and diagnosing some of the issues associated with payment and business verification.

WhatsApp Business Tools MCP is an expansion of Meta's strategy to use MCP servers, which allows AI agents to interact with third-party services and tools rather than just providing text answers.

Author:  @Colin
Post date: October 27, 2026, 9:04am UTC

Hi @Juliuscl,

This one is on Meta’s side. When you click Connect, Cursor tries to register itself as an OAuth client with Meta’s WhatsApp Business Tools server, and Meta refuses with “Dynamic registration is not available for this client” (it only pre-approves a few clients right now). Without that registration there’s no login page to open. The team knows about this limitation with Meta’s servers.

Meta Ads most likely works for you because that server has its own Client ID set. You can do the same for WhatsApp:

1. In your Meta app at developers.facebook.com, add `https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback` as a valid OAuth redirect URI.
2. On cursor.com/agents, edit the WhatsApp Business Tools server and enter the app’s App ID as the OAuth Client ID (and the App Secret as the Client Secret if your app uses one).
3. Click Connect again. The Facebook login window should open.
